findings.evidence: Statements at l. 240-241 (`μ.withDensity fun x => ENNReal.ofReal (f x)`) and l. 179 (`ENNReal.ofReal (min (f x) (c * g x) / c)`) versus docstrings at l. 236-237 ("the accepted variate has the law `f` normalised against `μ`") and l. 174 ("form the measure `μ` with density `min f (c * g) / c`"); the clipping convention is spelled out only at l. 99-100 and only for `g`.
findings.fix: Extend the `trialLaw` convention sentence (or add one to the module docstring) to say that `ENNReal.ofReal` reads negative values of the target `f` as `0` too, so "`f` normalised" means the positive part of `f` normalised; then the "no sign hypothesis" claims read honestly.
findings.issue: `trialLaw`'s docstring (l. 99-100) states the convention "Negative values of `g` are read as `0`", but nothing states it for `f`, while `map_fst_restrict_trialLaw_acceptSet` (l. 174-175) advertises "No bound and no sign hypothesis on `f` or `g` is needed". Every statement uses `ENNReal.ofReal (f x)` / `ENNReal.ofReal (min (f x) (c * g x))`, so for a sign-indefinite `f` the laws described as "`f` normalised" / density "`min f (c * g) / c`" are really the positive part. Same wording in the module docstring l. 33-34 and l. 43-44, and in `acceptedLaw_eq_smul_withDensity_of_ae_le` l. 236-237, `trialLaw_acceptSet_of_ae_le` l. 254-255, `isProbabilityMeasure_acceptedLaw_of_ae_le` l. 273-274, and the silent-bias conclusion "the accepted law is not `f` normalised" l. 295.

summary: Documentation is accurate and complete almost throughout, but the file documents the `ENNReal.ofReal` clipping convention for the proposal density `g` only, while simultaneously advertising that `f` needs no sign hypothesis — so the headline phrase "the accepted law is `f` normalised" is wrong exactly in the sign-indefinite case the docstrings promote.
